{"content":"## CPython 3.13’s Experimental Free-Threading Mode

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading as a configuration in which the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) can be disabled. In this mode, an application’s runtime choice connects directly to what happens when it imports an extension.

If an imported extension does not explicitly declare support for free threading, CPython issues a warning and enables the GIL. The way an extension makes that declaration depends on whether it uses multi-phase or single-phase initialization.

The declaration indicates support for the runtime mode; it does not establish that the extension’s code is thread-safe. Extension authors have a separate responsibility to make their code safe for use without the GIL."}
